quote: There's no wound on him, only the stiffness of the paralysis wearing off
why: In R64 the ghoul's claws did 6 damage to Bede ('Bede took 6: HP 11 -> 5') and R67 says 'Bede has 5 HP'. He has a real wound.

quote: he finally mutters something about honey and broth and puts the purse away
why: R74 had Garn press the purse into Brannoc's hand and said 'You have three silver pieces more than you had'. R75 has Garn take it back. R98 then explains the sheet by saying the silver 'went back into his own purse'.

quote: Your five candles still stand there in a row, burned low and replaced with fresh ones.
why: In R76/R77 the five candles are in Brannoc's pack ('tuck the blue skein and the five candles into my pack'), and R81 says 'You still have five candles', the ones left from Day 3. They can't also be standing in the lamp-house.

quote: The Ford Chapel is two hours up the road, about a mile past the ford.
why: R82/R83 put the chapel 'just past a ford', an hour from Greywater (R84 took 1h15 to walk back). Distance and ford relation both shift.

quote: You delivered all of it on Day 4
why: Hob's message for Maud ('tell Maud the lamp was lit', R79) was given on Day 7, not Day 4, and no scene shows it being delivered at Maud's later (R84, R88). The DM asserts it was passed on.

quote: was turned back at a flooded stretch of the causeway, so she's been trying to get home
why: Marta is walking up the causeway toward the hut, away from Reedholm (R102 'out of the dark... coming straight for the hut'), which is the opposite of trying to get home. Also she says she slept in this hut 'on the way out' two nights ago, yet Reedholm is a day and a half away.

quote: A crowd of spears wouldn't help much either
why: In round 128 the DM said 'Only the village fires would change that math.' In round 129 the village fires and spears are dismissed as useless, so the DM's earlier hint was false.

quote: She came up from the south as a girl
why: Pim says Wren came up from the south. Round 165 has the carters going north to Stonebridge, and round 138 had Wren a girl in Stonebridge. The DM's own note in round 144 says she came from the north.

In round 146 Wren says 'I stopped it a year ago. I didn't know they'd gone back to it'. In round 147 the game is said to have been started by Fen last month, after Jory's tale, so there was nothing to stop a year ago.

quote: the ford where it was lost is a mile back along the causeway
why: In round 143 Tamsin crossed the Black Ford and landed in Reedholm ('The Long House is the big hall by the landing'). Here the ford is a mile away, and in round 153 a 20-minute walk. Round 153 also never shows Tamsin crossing the channel that Pim's hut and punt sit on.

quote: Dawn's about six and a half hours of sleep away
why: Wren says six and a half hours, but at a quarter to ten the DM says dawn is 'about eight and three-quarter hours off'. The clock then jumps 8 h 45 m.
Tamsin arrived on Day 1 and it is Day 2 morning, so she has not seen the lights 'all week'.

quote: about a quarter of an hour away if you hurry
why: Round 156 describes the Isle as 'forty paces long'. Walking around it takes 12 minutes here, and Pim is a quarter hour away round the shore in rounds 158-161. Round 173 puts the wisps only 120 ft from the north crack.

quote: They are the same marks cut on the drowned-names post at the Long House.
why: Round 152 says the post has 'a small mark, a reed or a wave', and round 164 finds 'the reed and the wave, over and over, and no lamp at all'.

quote: tie the bundle to your back with the ferry-rope
why: In round 159 the ferry-rope is tied round a stone outside and 'the rope runs back to the stone' as a lifeline. In round 160 the same rope ties the bundle and is then 'under your hand' on the way out.

quote: I heard the horn go twice and stop.
why: Round 174 says 'You hear the horn on the landing once, short'.
